# Facilitator Guide — Safe & Responsible AI Use at Work

Slides: `slides/slides.md`. Demos: `demos/`. Exercise sheets: `exercises.md`. Every demo runs offline; start times assume 09:30.

**One week before:** run `python demos/run_all.py`. Confirm room, projector, one laptop per pair, Wi-Fi. Print exercises and handouts.

## Day 1

| Time | Segment | What you do and say |
|---|---|---|
| 09:30 | Welcome | Outcomes on the first slide. Ask each table for the one question they want answered; write them on the flipchart. |
| 09:40 | **Module 1 — Your AI policy in practice** | Teach: approved tools, prohibited data, disclosure. |
| 09:45 | Demo 1 | **Run `python demos/01_allowed_or_not.py`** — an AI-use policy written as data, applied to ten real situations with the rule that decided each. Close with: *“Two questions decide almost everything: is the tool approved, and what class of data is this?”* |
| 10:00 | Lab 1 | 10 scenarios: allowed or not? — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 10:12 | **Module 2 — Threats** | Teach: prompt injection, data leakage, deepfake fraud, shadow AI. |
| 10:17 | Demo 2 | **Run `python demos/02_spot_the_attack.py`** — eight inputs run through real controls (hidden-text stripping, injection classifier, PII redaction) and a red-flag checklist for a voice-clone payment request. Close with: *“You cannot hear a deepfake. You can always hear an unusual request. Verify the request, not the voice.”* |
| 10:32 | Lab 2 | Spot the attack — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 10:44 | **Module 3 — Incidents and escalation** | Teach: what counts as an incident, reporting path, human oversight. |
| 10:50 | Demo 3 | **Run `python demos/03_incident_triage.py`** — a triage rule set that turns a description into severity, owner, first actions and a filled incident report. Close with: *“Reporting fast is never the mistake. Hiding it for a week is.”* |
| 11:02 | Lab 3 | Report a mock incident — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 11:14 | Close | Assessment: Quiz ≥ 80%. Return to the flipchart questions — tick the ones answered. |

## If short on time

Keep every demo; shorten the teaching before it. Cut labs to a paired discussion of the lab question rather than dropping them. Never cut the close.

## What can go wrong

- **A demo fails on the day** — you ran `run_all.py` last week, so it is the environment: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then re-run. Screenshots of each output live in nobody's folder: take them after your dry run.
- **No projector / terminal too small** — open `/demos` in a browser and run the same demo from the *Course labs* section.
- **The room has no laptops** — run labs as table discussions using the printed exercise sheet; you run the script and change the inputs they call out.
